title: A fake supplier asks for payment to a new bank account

steps.situation: An email from "Shree Lab Supplies" says: "We have changed banks. Please pay this month's ₹1,80,000 invoice to our new account today." It came from shreelab-supplies.in. Last month's emails came from shreelabsupplies.in.

billing.text: Pay it to the new account: it's our regular supplier and the amount is right
billing.feedback: Scammers copy real invoices. A change of bank details is exactly when to check.

billing.text: Don't pay yet. Call the supplier on the number you already have and ask
billing.feedback: Right. A two-minute call on a number you already had stops this scam.

billing.text: Reply to the email and ask them to confirm
billing.feedback: Your reply goes to the scammer, who will happily "confirm".

steps.situation: The "supplier" phones the clinic: "Deliveries stop tomorrow unless you pay today. Don't call our old number, it's switched off."

billing.text: Pay now so deliveries don't stop
billing.feedback: Rushing you is the trick. A real supplier will wait for a quick check.

billing.text: Still don't pay. Check with a supplier contact you already have, and tell Dr. Rao
billing.feedback: Right. "Don't call our old number" is a warning sign on its own.

billing.text: Pay half now as a compromise
billing.feedback: Half to a scammer is still lost. Check first, pay nothing.

front_desk.text: Give the caller Ravi's mobile number so he can sort it out quickly
front_desk.feedback: Don't hand out staff details to a caller nobody has checked.

front_desk.text: Take a message and tell Ravi and Dr. Rao the caller is pushing for payment
front_desk.feedback: Right. Pressure to pay fast is worth passing on straight away.

owner.text: Tell Ravi to pay: you don't want trouble with the supplier
owner.feedback: A real supplier won't stop deliveries over a two-minute check.

owner.text: Tell Ravi: no payment to new bank details without your OK and a call to the supplier's old number
owner.feedback: Right. A simple rule like that stops this scam every time.

steps.situation: Ravi finds that a colleague paid ₹1,80,000 to the new account yesterday, after an email just like this one.

billing.text: Email the "supplier" asking for the money back
billing.feedback: They won't give it back. The bank and 1930 can freeze it; email can't.

billing.text: Call the bank right now to stop the payment, then call 1930
billing.feedback: Right. Soon after a payment, the bank and 1930 can often freeze the money before it is moved on.

billing.text: Wait until tomorrow to see if the real supplier asks for payment
billing.feedback: Every hour makes the money harder to freeze. Call the bank now.

owner.text: Keep it quiet to avoid embarrassment
owner.feedback: Speed matters more than embarrassment. The bank can only freeze money it hears about.

owner.text: Call the bank's fraud line with Ravi now and give them whatever they ask for
owner.feedback: Right. The account holder calling the bank speeds things up.

steps.situation: The bank has frozen part of the money.

billing.text: Delete the scam emails so nobody pays by mistake
billing.feedback: Those emails are the evidence. Keep them.

billing.text: Keep the emails and the payment receipt, and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in
billing.feedback: Right. The complaint helps the bank and police recover the rest.

front_desk.text: Write down when the caller rang and what he said, for Dr. Rao
front_desk.feedback: Right. Your notes add to the complaint.

front_desk.text: Nothing to do: it was a billing problem
front_desk.feedback: You spoke to the caller. What you remember is evidence.

owner.text: Nothing more to do: the bank has it now
owner.feedback: The complaint is what helps recover the rest of the money. Report it.

owner.text: Make sure the complaint is filed, and warn the real supplier their name was used
owner.feedback: Right. The real supplier can warn their other customers too.
